thread:
Anna (Marketing): Quick thread — thinking about the benchmark blog and webinar hook. What if we frame it as 'predictable inference economics' instead of just latency vs cost?
Carlos (Growth): Love that. Leads to better CTA for signups (predictable spend) vs cold numbers.
Jess (Product): Agree. Operational controls (batching, routing, fallback) should be the supporting proof points. Short bullets + 1 chart.
Liam (Data): For the chart, two small visuals: a scatter of latency vs tokens (actual runs) plus an inset waterfall showing cost per 1k tokens with/without caching. Keeps it concrete.
Noah (Design): I can mock a horizontal 'slices' chart that shows tail latency improvements at different qps. Want to avoid dense scatterplots — too noisy for landing copy.
Anna (Marketing): Good call. Main narrative: 1) predictable SLOs, 2) tuned economics, 3) graceful degradation. Each with one micro-chart and one customer quote.
Carlos (Growth): For inbound routing, can we add a form field that asks "primary constraint: latency / cost / compliance". Then route leads to the right track (hosted demo vs Dedicated sales).
Jess (Product): Yep — map to playbooks: latency -> real-time demo + dedicated, cost -> Optimize checklist + free eval credits, compliance -> Private onboarding.
Liam (Data): I can produce sample numbers from our internal bench: median latency @ 1k tokens, 99p tail, token cost delta w/ prefix caching. Will share CSV.
Noah (Design): Also recommend a single hero viz: a 3-column comparison (hosted / dedicated / private) with typical latency and $/1k token ranges. Simple.
Anna (Marketing): Copy idea for hero headline: "Inference you can budget for" with subhead: "Predictable latency and unit economics across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments." Thoughts?
Carlos (Growth): Nice. For webinar title: "How we cut inference unit cost without breaking latency" — maybe softer: "Balancing latency and cost: real tactics for production LLMs."
Jess (Product): Second title is better for broad audience. Keep the first as an exec summary line.
Anna (Marketing): Action items: Noah mock hero + 3 micro charts by Tue, Liam provide numbers by EOD tomorrow, Carlos wire up lead-routing fields, Jess provide 2 customer quotes we can anonymize. I'll draft blog intro.
Noah (Design): On it — will iterate on Slack thread with PNGs and a simplified SVG for marketing.
Liam (Data): Dropping CSV link when ready: https://redwood.internal/bench/1932156789-results.csv 
Carlos (Growth): I'll update the web form schema and add routing rules after Liam's numbers.
launch-bot: Reminder: marketing calendar slot reserved for 2026-04-07 webinar at 10am PT. :calendar:
